findings.claim: New sfcp-q27 reviewed. The key is correct and it is the only correct option. handleStatus treats 403 like 401: it calls forgetUser and goes to /sign-in with state.from = here. The taught sign-in ending, go(here.state?.from ?? '/', { replace: true }), copied verbatim from react/auth-and-review/handling-401-and-403-redirect-and-sign-out/artifact.md (cheat sheet) and artifact.html line ~344, sends Mia back to /admin/refunds. The API answers 403 again, so she loops back to sign-in. I re-ran the author's model (scratchpad/q27.mjs) on Node 24: key and all three rejections print PASS. All four feedback lines are accurate. A: the function has no 403 branch and never calls showNotAllowed. B: replace only swaps the history entry, and navigate state still carries from (react-router useNavigate). C, the key: 'Under the project contract a 403 keeps the user and shows not-allowed' matches the page's objectives o1/o3. D: the 401||403 branch matches. The topic is taught in full on both tracks (S34 and FT19, no '(skim)'), and blueprint #o2/#o3 match what the item tests. Minor cross-item cue: the stem states the server contract ('valid session but not the admin role ... the API answers 403'), and option A adds 'because the server answered 403, not 401'. Together they settle the 401-vs-403 sub-fact behind q08's '(a) 401, (b) 200, (c) 401' distractor. q08's main deciding fact, that the default JwtAuthenticationConverter ignores the roles claim, is untouched, and the q27 options only restate the general meaning the React page itself teaches. There is no leak with q20, which is about fetch rejection versus HTTP status, not auth handling.
